newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia big banks boom as bonds bounce back.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia big banks boom as bonds bounce back.

text.p: Shares in Australia's big banks headed for higher ground in trading on Wednesday as shaky bond markets, both locally and in the U.S., rebounded from Tuesday's battering.
Underlining the sector's strength, the banking index was up over 1.6 percent compared to gains in the benchmark All Ordinaries index of just 0.6 percent.
Commonwealth Bank shares and instalment receipts led the way, the shares adding 18 cents to A$10.78 while the ever-popular instalment receipts jumped 17 cents or over 2.5 percent to A$6.72.
Shares in Australia's largest bank, National Australia Bank Ltd, stormed home to close at its day's high, up 22 cents at A$12.28 on turnover of 1.54 million.

Among the other big banks, ANZ Bank Ltd shares closed seven cents higher at A$6.49 on turnover of 2.34 million shares while Westpac Banking Corporation shares saw a 2.5 percent gain to close 15 cents higher at A$6.17 on turnover of 3.46 million shares.
"The banks have been the star of the show with on the back of improved bonds," said a Sydney-based dealer.
The dealer singled out Commonwealth Bank instalment receipts as a strong performer, but added the whole sector still had plenty in it for investors in terms of dividend yield.
"CMG (instalment receipts) are showing no signs of stopping and there is always the yield attraction for the banks."
